quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #2
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What should you do to drive safely at night?

options.text: Increase your following distance.
Do not drive if you are tired.
Make sure your headlights work properly.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: At night, you cannot see as well. All of these steps help keep you and other drivers safe.

questions.question: Should drivers keep a safe distance from cyclists?

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Yes. Always keep a safe distance between your vehicle and any cyclist.

questions.question: What affects how long it takes to stop your car?

options.text: How fast you are driving.
The condition of your brakes and tires.
The condition of the road.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Your speed, your brakes and tires, and the road condition all affect stopping distance.

questions.question: What should you do when you see railroad tracks ahead?

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate comes down.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Do not worry about how many tracks you need to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always look and listen for trains. Slow down and be prepared to stop for trains or other vehicles on the tracks.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep driving because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down to stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what other cars next to you are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Turn quickly from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Keep driving until the next exit where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep driving until the next exit where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: Never back up on a freeway. Go to the next exit where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: You missed your freeway exit. What is the safest thing to do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Signal a police officer to escort you back.

questions.explanation: Go to the next exit. Do not stop, back up, or cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: The driver ahead is using one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Give that vehicle extra space.
Know the driver is not paying full attention to the road.
Do not copy that driver's behavior.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers are more likely to have accidents. Keep extra distance from them and always pay full attention to the road yourself.

questions.question: What should you do before you turn?

options.text: Use your turn signal.
Turn the wheel.
Speed up.
Change lanes.

questions.explanation: Turn on your signal 3 to 4 seconds before you turn. This tells other drivers what you plan to do.

questions.question: A school bus has stopped with its stop arm out. What must you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk and pass the bus on the left.
Keep driving once you think the kids are done getting off.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when a school bus shows its stop signal. Wait until the stop arm is raised before you drive.

questions.question: If someone is driving aggressively behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Stare at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: When you encounter an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact with them. Do not speed up or challenge them, as this will make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: What can reduce road rage and aggressive driving?

options.text: Allowing extra travel time.
Following posted speed limits.
Using turn signals.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: To help prevent road rage, use turn signals, follow speed limits, and allow plenty of time for your trip.

questions.question: A pedestrian starts to cross in front of your car. What should you do?

options.text: Flash your lights.
Slow down.
Speed up and pass in front of the pedestrian.
Stop and let the pedestrian cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and let the pedestrian cross.
questions.explanation: Always slow down and be ready to stop when you see pedestrians. Be extra careful around children. Let pedestrians cross in crosswalks.

questions.question: You are driving on the interstate and miss your exit. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to your exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your car in reverse to go back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn at your exit. If you miss your exit, continue to the next one.

questions.question: If you are in an accident, what should you do?

options.text: Stop your car at or near the scene.
Do not stand or walk in traffic lanes.
Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: After an accident, stop at or near the scene. Move your car out of traffic if you can. Stay out of traffic lanes to avoid being hit by other cars. Turn off the engines of damaged vehicles.

questions.question: What colors are used for warning signs about upcoming hazards?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background.
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.
White letters or symbols on a blue background.
White letters or symbols on a green background.

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black letters or symbols. Work zone warning signs are orange with black letters or symbols.

questions.question: You are approaching a railroad crossing and do not see or hear a train. When must you stop?

options.text: If a stop sign is posted.
If a crossing gate is down.
If the lights are flashing.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Always stop before crossing railroad tracks if red lights are flashing, the gate is down, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: When you leave your car unattended, what must you do?

options.text: Turn off the engine.
Lock the ignition and remove the key.
Set the parking brake.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When leaving your car unattended, turn off the engine, lock the ignition, remove the key, and set the parking brake.

questions.question: Driving involves risk. It is wise to keep improving your driving and observation skills.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Always work to improve your driving and observation skills. This keeps you and others safe. Never assume you have nothing left to learn.

questions.question: What is the only way to lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?

options.text: Drink coffee.
Exercise.
Wait for your body to process the alcohol over time.
Take a cold shower.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for your body to process the alcohol over time.
questions.explanation: Only time will lower your BAC. Coffee, exercise, and cold showers cannot reduce your BAC or make you sober. They may help you stay awake, but they do not change your blood alcohol level.

questions.question: When driving on major highways, what should you do?

options.text: Stay alert.
Keep your eyes moving.
Be ready to react to road hazards.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: On highways, you must stay alert and be ready to react to unexpected dangers. Keep your eyes moving to avoid staring at one thing too long. This helps prevent "highway hypnosis."

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you that you cannot drive in your current direction.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing?

options.text: Slow down.
Look for a train.
Be ready to stop.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When you see signs for a railroad crossing, slow down and look for a train. Be ready to stop. If red lights are flashing or the gate is down, stop 15 to 50 feet before the tracks. Never try to go around the gate.

questions.question: How can you prevent fatigue on a long drive?

options.text: Stop and rest every two hours.
Do arm exercises every hour.
Drive with one eye open at a time.
Change feet on the gas pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and rest every two hours.
questions.explanation: Stop every two hours to take a short break on long trips. If you feel drowsy, pull over safely and nap or find a place to stay for the night.

questions.question: If a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone, you must:

options.text: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
Copy what surrounding traffic is doing, despite the crossing guard's instructions.
Assume the guard is not supposed to be directing traffic.
Follow rules that would be in place if no children were present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow the directions given by the crossing guard.
questions.explanation: Always follow the directions of a crossing guard, sign, or police officer. Always drive slowly and carefully in school zones.
